scope: Proposition 6.1 of the manuscript “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (preprints/Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime-two-October-6-2026/two-adic-promodularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ef74b48557930663), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let rx : GQ,S → GL2(Ex) be odd, absolutely irreducible, and classical cuspidal up to Tate twist. Suppose its restriction to GQ2 is absolutely irreducible and de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, and its Weil–Deligne representation is trivial on wild inertia. Here S is any finite set containing 2 and all ramified primes. Then dimEx H1 (GQ,S, ad rx) ≤ 3. Consequently, if Rglob is the universal global determinant deformation ring with varying determinant for the semisimplified residual data of rx, and x is its coefficient prime, then edim(Rglob)x ≤ 3. Both assertions permit scalar or reducible semisimplified residual data and finite extension of the coefficient ring.
